title: Polynomial-Time Second-Component Mapping
statement: Let $g$ be a polynomial-time computable function on bit strings. The function that, on input $z$, decodes $z$ as a pair $(a,b)$ and returns the encoding of $(a,g(b))$ when decoding succeeds, and the empty string when it fails, is polynomial-time computable.
replaced:
If a function $g$ on binary strings is polynomial-time computable, then so is the
function that decodes its input as a pair $(a, b)$, returns the pair encoding of
$a$ with $g(b)$, and returns the empty word when the input is not a valid pair
encoding.
